purpose: silver_flights holds one row per scheduled commercial flight departing from a New York City area airport (EWR, JFK, or LGA) between 2013-01-01 and 2013-06-30, combining carrier identity, scheduled and actual departure/arrival times, delay and cancellation status, aircraft attributes looked up by tail number, and origin/destination airport reference attributes.
usage: Read the table at the grain of (flight_date, carrier_code, flight_number, origin_airport): each row is one scheduled flight. Check is_cancelled before interpreting dep_hhmm, arr_hhmm, dep_delay_minutes, arr_delay_minutes, and air_time_minutes, since these carry nulls (roughly 2.9% to 3.3% null) when a flight did not complete. Aircraft attribute columns (aircraft_manufacturer, aircraft_model, aircraft_manufacture_year, aircraft_seat_count, aircraft_engine_type) are null for about 16-18% of rows where the tail_number lookup did not resolve. Destination airport reference columns are null for about 2.1% of rows.
limitations: The profile cannot independently confirm that (flight_date, carrier_code, flight_number, origin_airport) uniquely identifies a row; only a deterministic grain measurement against the warehouse can confirm this, and tail_number, which would narrow the grain further, is itself 0.9154% null. The relationship between sched_dep_hour_local/sched_dep_minute_local and sched_dep_hhmm, and between departure_hour_utc and the local schedule fields, is inferred from samples and not verified by the profile. The captured_at column's values (dated 2026-09-02, a narrow 16-second span) are inconsistent with the 2013 flight data and look like a pipeline load timestamp even though the profile marks is_airbyte_metadata false; a reviewer should confirm its intended meaning and whether it belongs in this table's business grain.
